viewpoints.en: wide-angle corner view showing the entire room layout
eye-level medium shot focused on a furniture cluster
macro close-up of wall/floor materials and textures
close-up of hardware, fixtures or lighting details
bird's-eye overhead shot of the whole space
shot framed through or from the window side
one-point perspective shot from the doorway looking in

camera_moves_4s.en: [0s-4s]: smooth slow push-in (dolly forward) revealing the room, ending on a refined composition
[0s-4s]: slow pull-out from a detail to reveal the full space, gentle and cinematic
[0s-4s]: smooth horizontal pan from left to right across the room at eye level
[0s-4s]: slow orbital arc around the focal furniture piece, parallax depth
[0s-4s]: slow tilt-up from floor materials to ceiling and lighting design
[0s-4s]: static locked-off frame with a slow rack focus shift between foreground and background

shot_planning_prompt:
You are a senior interior design videographer and AI prompt engineer.

TASK: Plan exactly {num_shots} distinct shots that recreate the SAME interior design style in DIFFERENT rooms and viewpoints, for use as 4-second stock footage clips.

INPUTS:
- STYLE LOCK (every shot MUST preserve this style): {style_descriptor_en}
- Available room types: {room_options}
- Available viewpoints: {viewpoint_options}
- Available 4s camera moves: {camera_options}

PLANNING RULES:
1. Pick exactly {num_shots} shots. Each shot = one (room_type, viewpoint, camera_move) combination.
2. DIVERSITY: maximize variety across rooms and viewpoints. Do NOT repeat the same room more than twice. Cover at least 4 different room types. Cover at least 4 different viewpoints. Use at least 4 different camera moves.
3. STYLE CONSISTENCY: every shot MUST look like it belongs to the SAME home/project — same color palette, same materials, same furniture language, same lighting mood described in the STYLE LOCK.
4. REALISM: rooms must be physically plausible and internally consistent (real furniture scale, correct lighting, sensible layout). No floating objects, no impossible geometry.
5. Each shot must be a COMPLETE, self-contained 4-second clip (not a continuation of another).

OUTPUT FORMAT — return ONLY a JSON array of {num_shots} objects, no markdown:
[
  {
    "shot_id": 1,
    "room_type": "living_room",
    "viewpoint": "wide_corner",
    "camera_move": "slow_push_in",
    "image_prompt": "A complete English prompt describing the still image: [STYLE LOCK phrases] + this specific room + this viewpoint + composition + lighting + materials + no people. 80-150 words.",
    "video_prompt": "A complete English prompt for the 4-second clip: start from the [camera_move template] + describe the specific motion of this scene + keep style consistent. 60-100 words."
  }
]

CRITICAL: the image_prompt and video_prompt must EACH contain the STYLE LOCK key phrases (materials, palette, lighting) so the generator preserves style. Never include people unless the style explicitly calls for it (default: empty interior, no people).
